cards.front: Why is a dish containing 600 measured cells still one experiment when the whole dish receives one condition?
cards.back: All cells share the assigned condition and are not independent experimental units; the dish is the single experimental unit.
cards.quote: The film's opening dish was one experiment per condition, not 600: every cell shared its dish

cards.front: A p-value measures incompatibility with a specified {{c1::no-effect model}}.
cards.quote: the reported p-value—a measure of incompatibility with a specified no-effect model—used the wrong units

cards.front: {{c1::Quiescent}} cells are not actively cycling.
cards.quote: Quiescent cells are not actively cycling. Wnt proteins are secreted signals.
cards.section: Make the models disagree

cards.front: Why should completed division, rather than S-phase entry, be the primary endpoint when testing the two stretch models?
cards.back: Both models predict S-phase entry, but only Model A predicts completion without Wnt; division is where their predictions disagree.
cards.quote: Because the models agree at S-phase entry and disagree at division, completion is the primary endpoint.
cards.section: Make the models disagree

cards.front: Before collecting data, how should competing models and an inconclusive outcome be built into an experimental test?
cards.back: Give each model a numerical prediction for the chosen endpoint and predefine the range that favors neither. This makes disconfirmation possible.
cards.why: The design rests on the rule that an experiment able only to confirm a model is not a test.
cards.quote: Before collecting an image, write each model's numerical prediction for the chosen endpoint and the range that would favour neither.
cards.section: Make the models disagree

cards.front: Wnt3A alone produces as many completed divisions as stretch plus Wnt3A. What happens to Model B's cooperation claim, and why?
cards.back: It fails. Stretch adds nothing in Wnt3A medium, whereas Model B predicts that stretch should add at least 10 percentage points more there than in control medium.
cards.quote: If Wnt3A alone matches stretch plus Wnt3A, stretch adds nothing in Wnt3A medium.
cards.section: Make the models disagree

cards.front: Why must a two-by-two test of stretch and Wnt3A include a Wnt3A-alone arm?
cards.back: It distinguishes Wnt3A merely adding divisions on its own from Wnt3A cooperating with stretch to complete the cycle.
cards.quote: This is why the Wnt3A-alone arm is required.
cards.section: Make the models disagree

cards.front: Fucci means {{c1::fluorescent ubiquitination-based cell-cycle indicator}}.
cards.quote: Fucci means fluorescent ubiquitination-based cell-cycle indicator.
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: In the described MDCK cells, red mKO2-Cdt1 marks {{c1::G0 and G1}}.
cards.back: Green mAG-Geminin marks cells from S phase until mitosis.
cards.quote: In these MDCK cells, red mKO2-Cdt1 marks G0 and G1
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: In the described MDCK cells, green mAG-Geminin marks cells from {{c1::S phase until mitosis}}.
cards.quote: green mAG-Geminin marks cells from S phase, when DNA is copied, until mitosis
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: Why does a green Fucci cell not by itself show that cell division was completed?
cards.back: Green roughly marks entry into S phase through mitosis; only tracking the cell to an observed division directly shows completion here.
cards.quote: a green cell has roughly entered S, while only the path to an observed division directly shows completion here
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: During its labelling window, cells incorporate the thymidine analogue {{c1::EdU}} into DNA.
cards.back: EdU is an endpoint for DNA synthesis, not a direct division count.
cards.quote: EdU supplies a separate endpoint: it is a thymidine analogue that cells build into DNA during the labelling window.
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: What does agreement between green Fucci and EdU support, and what does it not establish?
cards.back: It supports entry into S phase, but neither measure becomes a count of completed divisions.
cards.quote: agreement between green Fucci and EdU supports entry into S without turning either measure into a division count
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: Green cells begin rising after about 8 hours. A cell enters S at hour 20, and observation stops at hour 24. Can the record rule out its later division, and why?
cards.back: No. It cannot finish S, G2, and mitosis within the remaining four hours, so the negative result applies only to the observed window.
cards.quote: A cell that enters S at 20 hours cannot finish S, G2 and mitosis by 24 hours.
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: Two circular tissues have initial radii 850 and 1,700 micrometres. Each edge moves outward 30 micrometres per hour for 10 hours. What are their percentage area increases?
cards.back: The radii become 1,150 and 2,000 micrometres. Thus (1150/850)² - 1 = 0.83, or 83%, and (2000/1700)² - 1 = 0.38, or 38%.
cards.quote: Their radii move from 850 to 1,150 micrometres and from 1,700 to 2,000.
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: Two circular tissues expand at the same constant edge speed, but the smaller one has a larger percentage area increase. Does that prove faster proliferation, and why?
cards.back: No. Radius enters area quadratically, so geometry alone can create different percentage area increases; no division rate appears in that calculation.
cards.quote: Geometry alone creates the difference, so percent area growth does not prove proliferation.
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: A spreading epithelial tissue shows a large increase in area. What measurements would distinguish geometric spreading from proliferation?
cards.back: Count nuclei and track individual divisions in addition to measuring area. The rule is that area growth alone contains no division rate.
cards.why: This combines the geometry warning with direct cell-number and division endpoints.
cards.quote: Count nuclei, as microscopy and images describes, and track divisions.
cards.section: Read the endpoint before interpreting it

cards.front: What is an experimental unit?
cards.back: The thing independently assigned to a condition, such as a dish, stretch device, or mouse.
cards.quote: the experimental unit is the thing independently assigned to a condition: a dish, stretch device or mouse
cards.section: Read repeatability at the independent-unit level

cards.front: What is an observational unit?
cards.back: The thing measured, such as a cell or field.
cards.quote: The observational unit is what is measured: a cell or field.
cards.section: Read repeatability at the independent-unit level

cards.front: N is the number of {{c1::experimental units}}.
cards.back: It is not the number of cells or fields measured within a shared treatment unit.
cards.quote: N is the number of experimental units (Lazic and colleagues, 2018).
cards.section: Read repeatability at the independent-unit level

cards.front: Why is treating cells from one dish as independent replicates pseudoreplication?
cards.back: The cells share one independently assigned treatment unit, so they do not provide independent treatment repetitions.
cards.quote: Treating cells that share a dish as independent replicates is pseudoreplication.
cards.section: Read repeatability at the independent-unit level

cards.front: A drug is assigned to whole wells, and 300 cells are imaged per well. What is the experimental unit, and what are the observational units?
cards.back: Each well is an experimental unit because treatment was assigned by well; the imaged cells are observational units.
cards.quote: The observational unit is what is measured: a cell or field.
cards.section: Read repeatability at the independent-unit level

cards.front: Three independent days each contain one control and one treated dish, with 200 cells scored per dish. What is N per condition?
cards.back: N = 3 per condition. Each day supplies one independently treated dish per condition; the 200 cells are observations within that unit.
cards.quote: Each of three independent days has one control dish and one treated dish, with 200 cells scored per dish for EdU.
cards.section: Worked problem: six hundred cells, three runs

cards.front: Why should dish summaries retain their run labels instead of pooling all scored cells?
cards.back: Dish summaries preserve run-to-run disagreement, while pooling erases it and can hide poor repeatability.
cards.quote: Pooling erases the run labels. Runs 1 and 3 show large differences; run 2 barely moves.
cards.section: Worked problem: six hundred cells, three runs

cards.front: A paired analysis gives p = 0.13 with a wide interval. Is 'there is no effect' justified, and what should be concluded?
cards.back: No. The runs leave the effect uncertain; a non-significant result does not demonstrate no effect, and the wide interval displays that uncertainty.
cards.quote: A non-significant result does not show no effect, and the wide interval makes the uncertainty visible.
cards.section: Worked problem: six hundred cells, three runs

cards.front: If each of three dishes is rescored from 200 to 2,000 cells, what happens to N and to run-to-run uncertainty?
cards.back: N remains 3. Counting noise may shrink, but extra cells from the same dishes do not remove run-to-run variation; more independent runs address it.
cards.quote: Scoring 2,000 cells per dish would shrink some counting noise, but N would remain three and run-to-run variation would remain.
cards.section: Worked problem: six hundred cells, three runs

cards.front: What handling control is needed for a stretch-device experiment, and what alternative explanation does it address?
cards.back: Assemble, mount, and image unstretched devices identically. This separates stretch from differences caused by handling.
cards.quote: Handling: assemble, mount and image unstretched devices identically, or "stretch" includes every handling difference.
cards.section: Controls that rule out the boring explanations

cards.front: What is the correct control for a drug dissolved in a vehicle?
cards.back: Use the solvent without drug at the same concentration.
cards.quote: Drug: match the vehicle—the drug's solvent without drug—at the same concentration.
cards.section: Controls that rule out the boring explanations

cards.front: Why does copying an inhibitor concentration from a paper not establish the drug's potency in a new experiment?
cards.back: A copied concentration is only an experimental condition; it is not itself a measurement of potency.
cards.quote: A concentration copied from a paper is a condition, not a measure of potency.
cards.section: Controls that rule out the boring explanations

cards.front: Which observer controls reduce condition-dependent scoring bias?
cards.back: Fix positivity thresholds before analysis, score blind to condition, and apply the same thresholds to every condition.
cards.quote: fix positivity thresholds before analysis, score blind to condition and keep thresholds the same across conditions
cards.section: Controls that rule out the boring explanations

cards.front: Why must investigators measure the strain cells actually experience and restrict analysis to the strained region?
cards.back: Measure the strain cells actually experience, analyze only the strained region, and do not merge devices that impose different strains.
cards.quote: Stretch: measure the strain cells actually feel and analyze only the strained region.
cards.section: Controls that rule out the boring explanations

cards.front: TOPdGFP reports {{c1::beta-catenin-dependent transcription}}.
cards.back: It is a destabilized GFP driven by beta-catenin-responsive sites.
cards.quote: TOPdGFP is a destabilized GFP driven by beta-catenin-responsive sites; it reports beta-catenin-dependent transcription
cards.section: Controls that rule out the boring explanations

cards.front: One inhibitor yields the expected phenotype. What addition best tests whether loss of the intended target caused it, and why?
cards.back: Perturb the target genetically, then rescue with a version the perturbation cannot touch. This tests the target independently of the drug's off-target effects.
cards.quote: Use an independent genetic perturbation of the target, then restore the target with a rescue version the perturbation cannot touch.
cards.section: Controls that rule out the boring explanations

cards.front: Design the treatment structure and assignment for testing whether stretch and Wnt3A cooperate in MDCK cells.
cards.back: Use a 2 × 2 factorial: no stretch or stretch crossed with parental L-cell or Wnt3A-conditioned medium. Run all arms each day and randomly assign devices within day.
cards.why: The four arms estimate each input alone and together; within-day randomization supports a day-paired comparison.
cards.quote: Run all four arms on each day, assigning devices to arms at random within the day.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: Define a primary endpoint that directly tests whether initially quiescent cells complete division after stretch.
cards.back: Predefine Q as the fraction red at the start that are tracked through green to an observed division in a window covering delayed S entry plus S, G2, and M.
cards.why: This applies the rule that cycle entry is not completion and that the observation window must cover the relevant delay.
cards.quote: The fraction of cells red at the start that are tracked through green (S/G2) to an observed division within a set window
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: Using Q as completed division, what numerical outcomes favor Model A, Model B, or neither?
cards.back: Model A: stretch minus control is at least 10 points. Model B: stretch minus control is at most 2, and the stretch effect in Wnt3A medium is at least 10 points larger than in control medium. Between 2 and 10 favors neither.
cards.why: These are the lesson's invented teaching thresholds for making the competing models falsifiable.
cards.quote: Inconclusive: a stretch-alone difference between 2 and 10 points, or confidence intervals wide enough to fit both models.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: How should independent runs be analyzed and displayed in the redesigned four-arm experiment?
cards.back: Analyze day-paired device means and display the independent run summaries as a SuperPlot; N is the number of independent days.
cards.why: This combines the unit rule with the paired design: cells are observations, whereas independent days supply repeatability.
cards.quote: Analysis. Day-paired device means, shown as a SuperPlot.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: A result supports Model B in quiescent canine MDCK-II monolayers under static strain. Can it be generalized directly to another epithelium or stretch regime?
cards.back: No. A different starting state, stretch type, epithelium, or tissue requires a separate experiment.
cards.why: The conclusion's scope is limited by the biological system and perturbation actually tested.
cards.quote: Whether the same holds with another starting state, another kind of stretch, another epithelium or in tissue is a separate experiment.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: Why can red Fucci fluorescence not prove that a cell is quiescent?
cards.back: Red Fucci does not distinguish G0 from G1.
cards.quote: Red Fucci does not distinguish G0 from G1, so red alone cannot prove that a cell is quiescent.
cards.section: Reporter limits and biological scope

cards.front: How does the Fucci dark period bias a snapshot taken after mitosis?
cards.back: Neither color is bright just after mitosis, so the snapshot undercounts cells that have just divided.
cards.quote: The construct also has a dark period after mitosis, when neither color is bright
cards.section: Reporter limits and biological scope

cards.front: Independent paired differences are 6, 10, 2, and 6 percentage points. What are the mean difference and its standard error?
cards.back: Mean = 24/4 = 6 points. Deviations are 0, 4, -4, 0; sample variance = 32/3, SD = 3.27, and SE = 3.27/√4 = 1.63 points.
cards.quote: With the dish as the unit, the last column of the table has mean 29 / 3 = 9.67 points.
cards.section: The paired calculation

cards.front: For paired dish differences 14, 2, and 13 percentage points, calculate the mean, sample SD, and standard error.
cards.back: Mean = 29/3 = 9.67 points. Squared deviations sum to 88.7; SD = √(88.7/2) = 6.66, and SE = 6.66/√3 = 3.84 points.
cards.quote: Dividing by n − 1 gives variance 44.3, SD 6.66 and SE 6.66 / sqrt(3) = 3.84.
cards.section: The paired calculation
